disposition_reason: A methods paper that prints lead means for one unspiked wheat bread sample by two techniques; monitoring results are only a share distribution.

study.design: Laboratory method comparison (stripping voltammetry vs AAS) with spike additions, plus summary of routine monitoring
study.period_text: Monitoring of bread results January 2019 to October 2020; validation sample date not stated
study.method: Stripping voltammetry (TA-4 analyzer) and atomic absorption spectrometry (Kvant-2AT)
study.lod_text: TA-4 range from 0.005 or 0.01 mg/kg depending on electrode
study.qa: Additions of 0.03 mg/kg at sample-preparation and measurement stages; repeatability Sr 18% (AAS) and 13% (voltammetry); no CRM

findings.group: single bread sample, stripping voltammetry (TA-4 analyzer), unspiked
findings.notes: Mean of five repeat determinations of one wheat bread sample used for method validation; replicates 0.011, 0.0094, 0.0101, 0.0113, 0.0107; unit inferred from table title (permissible concentration 0.5 mg/kg)

findings.group: single bread sample, atomic absorption (Kvant-2AT), unspiked
findings.notes: Mean of five repeat determinations of the same bread sample; replicates 0.011, 0.013, 0.015, 0.0095, 0.01; Table 5 gives the two-method mean 0.0111

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Permissible Pb level cited for wheat bread (TR CU 021/2011)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 0.5 mg/kg (Table 3 title); Table 5 title states 0.15 mg/kg

unresolved: Spiked results (Tables 3-5, additions 0.03 or 0.05 mg/kg) are QA, not findings
Monitoring 2019-2020: 75.6% of wheat bread results below 0.01 mg/kg and 2.2% in 0.1-1.0 mg/kg; number of samples not stated and the distribution is figure-only (Figure 6)
Laboratory location and bread origin not stated
Tables 3 and 5 cite different permissible levels (0.5 vs 0.15 mg/kg)
